# Extending

This chapter covers the ways to add capabilities to an agent: skills, subagents, hooks, and MCP servers.

## Skills

- Skills are re-usable prompts.  Rather than retyping detailed instructions to perform some repeated task, you can invoke skills with slash commands.
- E.g. `/clear` wipes the context from the session.
- **Claude is good at writing its own skills**.  Examples:
  - "create a `/wildfire-news` skill to find the top wildfire-related news stories in the last few days.  The user should be able to specify the region of interest and number of days.  Create an HTML report with links to the original articles."  Afterwards try `/wildfire-news Denver 7 days`.
  - "create a `/primer` skill to research a subject and get me up to speed on it."  Then: `Give me a /primer on the state of the art of wildfire propagation modeling`.

## Subagents

- Claude and Codex can spawn subagents to "work for" the one you're having a session with.  They will do this themselves or you can specifically instruct them to do so.
  - "Analyze the approach of my fire model.  Spawn agents to compare and contrast my model with state-of-the-art open source wildfire modeling projects."

## Hooks

- A hook is a command the tool runs at a fixed event: before a tool call, after a file edit, when the agent finishes.
- Instructions files are requests.  Hooks are enforced.  "Never edit `.env`" in `CLAUDE.md` can be ignored; a hook that blocks the edit cannot.
- Examples: run the formatter after each edit, block `git commit` unless the tests passed.
  - Block at commit rather than at each write.  Blocking mid-task can confuse the agent.
- In Claude Code, hooks live in `.claude/settings.json` and `/hooks` lists them.  The agent can write them for you.

## Model Context Protocol (MCP)

- An MCP server connects the agent to an external service (issue tracker, database, browser) by giving it new tools.
- Add one with `claude mcp add` or `codex mcp add`.
- Each server costs context.  If a command-line tool already exists (`gh`, `aws`, `psql`), the agent can use it with no setup.  Add a server only when it removes a manual step, e.g. copying data out of a browser tab.
- Vendors do not audit third-party servers.  Install only ones you trust.

## Which one to use

| Situation | Mechanism |
|---|---|
| You corrected the same thing twice | Instructions file |
| You retype the same prompt | Skill |
| A side task floods the conversation | Subagent |
| Something must happen every time | Hook |
| The agent needs data from an external service | CLI tool, else MCP server |
| A second project needs the same setup | Plugin (a bundle of the above) |
